result.title: Any Forcing: Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability for Autoregressive Video Generation
result.summary: Autoregressive video generation enables efficient inference through streaming prediction. However, existing methods are typically restricted to fixed sampling steps, limiting the flexibility to balance generation quality and efficiency, while one-step generation suffers from degraded visual quality and error accumulation over long sequences, leading to content drift and generation collapse. To address these issues, we propose Any Forcing, a unified framework for achieving Any-Step Generality and One-Step Stability. Specifically, we introduce a unified adversarial discriminator that jointly performs real-distribution alignment, inter-step consistency alignment, and first-frame quality enhancement, enabling flexible sampling while preserving one-step generation quality. Furthermore, we propose a training-free adaptive long-term memory selection mechanism that selects historical states based on global semantic relevance and local value contribution, while remapping their temporal positions to preserve temporal relationships within the memory cache, thereby enabling stable one-step long-video generation. Experiments demonstrate that Any Forcing achieves high-quality and stable one-step autoregressive video generation, achieving 20.9 FPS and 24.7 FPS for short and long video generation on a single H100 GPU, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Any Forcing 框架，用统一对抗判别器兼顾真实分布对齐、步间一致性与首帧质量，实现任意步采样下的一步生成质量；并提出免训练的自适应长期记忆选择机制，按全局语义相关性与局部价值贡献挑选历史状态并重映射其时间位置，以稳定长视频的一步自回归生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属自回归视频生成，与视觉推理无直接关联；但其「按相关性与贡献筛选历史状态＋位置重映射」的免训练缓存机制，可能为多步 latent 推理中的状态与缓存筛选、以及步间一致性监督提供可供核查的线索。
